name: Swan Defence and Heavy Industries Ltd (formerly Reliance Naval and Engineering Ltd)
tagline: Pipavav shipyard/heavy-engineering asset that emerged from a multi-year insolvency process (NCLT resolution plan approved Dec 2022, new Swan Energy/Hazel Mercantile promoters took control Jan 2024, renamed Jan 2025, full creditor repayment completed March 2026) - a real defence/shipbuilding tailwind story, but still loss-making with extreme leverage.
business_overview: Owns and operates one of India's largest integrated shipbuilding and heavy-engineering complexes at Pipavav, Gujarat - originally built by Reliance Naval & Engineering (formerly Pipavav Defence), which went through Corporate Insolvency Resolution starting ~2020. Swan Energy Ltd's group (via Hazel Mercantile) won the NCLT-approved resolution bid (~Rs 2,100 Cr, Dec 2023/approved Dec 2022 plan), took management control Jan 2024, and renamed the entity Swan Defence and Heavy Industries (SDHI) in Jan 2025. All Committee-of-Creditors dues were fully repaid by March 2026 - the company is out of active CIRP. It is now positioned as a Make-in-India defence/commercial shipbuilding and offshore-heavy-engineering platform, riding the broader domestic naval/shipbuilding capex tailwind (alongside peers like GRSE, Cochin Shipyard, Mazagon Dock).
fundamentals_table: Q4 FY26 sales ~Rs 236 Cr (reported +4712% YoY off a near-nil base); consolidated net loss ~Rs 142 Cr same quarter
Net debt ~Rs 2,436 Cr (Mar-26); debt/equity ~635% - very high leverage
Resolution plan fully executed; full creditor repayment completed March 2026; no longer under CIRP
fundamentals_narrative: This is a post-insolvency turnaround, not a going-concern red flag anymore - the NCLT process concluded years ago, new promoters (Swan Energy group) have controlled and funded it since Jan 2024, and all creditor obligations were discharged by March 2026. That said, the balance sheet remains genuinely weak on a standalone basis: revenue is still ramping from a near-zero base, the company posted a large net loss as recently as the March 2026 quarter, ROE has averaged -48.9% over three years, and net debt-to-equity of ~635% is extreme even for a capital-intensive shipyard. The defence/shipbuilding sector tailwind (Atmanirbhar Bharat, naval modernisation) is real and shared with better-capitalised peers (GRSE, Cochin Shipyard, Mazagon Dock), but SDHI itself has not yet demonstrated a profitable, de-levered operating record post-resolution.
